$comment: R1886 — THE BEHAVIOUR CANON'S INTERACTION SURFACE, as a derived census.
Read `tools/canon_surface_census.py` for what each field means and what is
checked. This file is the pin; the tool is the reader; the walk named in
`proven_by` is what makes a verdict a measurement rather than a mark.
WHY IT EXISTS. This census lived as a hand-counted table in a session note
for 164 rounds. The note said so itself, in as many words: `산문이다` — it
is prose — and prescribed exactly this file. Two things had already gone
wrong in the meantime, and R1886 found both by re-deriving the table:
1. The note's stated extraction procedure DID NOT REPRODUCE ITS OWN
NUMBERS. It says to strip the document's `<script>` elements and
count; done that way six of its fourteen rows come out ZERO, because
the canon's event bindings are template-DSL attributes rather than
`on*` ones. Every number in the note is right and the recipe under it
is wrong, which is the worst arrangement: a reader who follows the
recipe concludes the canon binds no presses at all.
2. Two of its `have` marks were wrong in the direction that hides work.
The tooltip row and the hover row were ticked on the framework's
ability rather than on the application's use of it — see the two rows
below that now read `gap`, each naming the debt it opened.
WHAT THE POPULATION IS. A GESTURE, not an event name. The canon is a web
document and spells one gesture with three event families (mouse, pointer,
HTML5 drag) because that platform has three; this tree has one pointer
model. A row per event name would therefore report three gaps where there
is one gesture, so a row is a gesture and its `probes` are every token the
canon spends on it. The counts still add up, and the completeness rule
below is what keeps the grouping honest.
COMPLETENESS, which the prose census asserted and could not check. The
word it used was 전수 — exhaustive — and nothing re-derived it. Now:
`--extract` refuses the canon if any declarative handler attribute, any
runtime listener, or any markup attribute at all is neither claimed by a
row's `probes` nor classified in `inert` with a reason. An attribute
nobody classified is RED, not silence.
NDA. The tokens below are the prototype's own template-DSL spelling and
carry no domain, product, protocol or customer word; the counts are counts.
The document itself is not in this repository and never will be.

document.what: the behaviour canon's document markup, with every `<script>` element removed

rows.surface: a press on an element causes that element's operation
rows.covered_by: every affordance of every section is a hit-testable painted rectangle whose press resolves to itself; the shell routes a press through one pointer model rather than three event families

rows.surface: a press, a move and a release move or resize the thing under the cursor
rows.covered_by: a card's grip drags it to another cell, a detached panel drags by its bar and resizes by its corner; the canon's three event families are one gesture here

rows.surface: a thing is picked up on one surface and let go on another, and the destination says where it would land
rows.covered_by: the palette hands the board a footprint: a row is picked up, the board previews the cell, and letting go places it there or refuses

rows.surface: typing into a field changes what the field holds as each character arrives
rows.covered_by: the application bar's search field takes characters and backspaces as they are typed, and the capture viewer's filter and the lab inspector's rows are edit fields on the same lifted keymap

rows.surface: opening a roster on a value control and pressing an option writes that option
rows.covered_by: a collapsing selection control: the preferences page's value rows open a roster in the control's own column, and pressing an option writes it and shuts the roster

rows.surface: a wheel over the graph canvas zooms it about the cursor
rows.covered_by: the node lab canvas answers the wheel hook and declines where it has nothing to spend, and it answers it as a mounted section of the assembled tool rather than only as its own binary

rows.surface: an empty field shows what would go in it
rows.covered_by: an empty field's placeholder is painted inside the field's own box and holds its own letters

rows.surface: resting on a control shows a sentence about it that the control has no room to print
rows.covered_by: R1916 — a mark carries a sentence (pinion_core::describe::Descriptions) and one derivation says which one a reader is being shown, from hover OR focus in one call. The node lab's pins are the first consumer: resting on one draws the sentence beside it and announces it, with the pin pointing at the region through aria-describedby so nothing dangles. What the framework had was a tooltip that was its OWN anchor -- R695's module docs name 'attach a tooltip to an arbitrary existing widget' as a future axis, which is why the widget existed and no screen mounted one. Past the canon: the sentence is COMPOSED by the model (Document::port_tooltip joins what the type says it carries with what the port says it is for) rather than authored per control, and a split member says which half it is. The canon's own twenty-five are static title attributes, and R1918 measured where they sit: NINE are on the chrome (the icon rail's eight seats and the appearance toggle, drawn at every destination) and the rest are spread over its pages. R1918 covers all six pages of the assembled tool -- every Page destination names at least one described mark of its OWN, and the walk checks each is painted inside that destination's page rectangle so the chrome cannot satisfy the claim for a page that says nothing. Every sentence is DERIVED from the declaration its mark is built from (a column carries its own description, a severity choice derives one from the floor it filters by, a rail seat from the requirement it is booked under), so a column added later cannot compile without saying what it holds

rows.surface: a control changes appearance while the cursor rests on it, before any press
rows.covered_by: R1916 — the same mechanism as affordance.tooltip, which is what made this closeable in one round rather than two: pinion_core::describe carries a sentence per mark and one derivation says which one a reader is being shown, so a cursor coming to rest CHANGES THE FRAME. The shell describes its own icon chrome (a card's move grip, its widen seat) — the canon's rule for which controls get a title is the ones with no room to print what they do — and the node lab describes its pins. Past the canon: the same call answers for KEYBOARD FOCUS, so the hover affordance does not arrive as a pointer-only regression on a tree that already has focus rings; the canon has zero key bindings and copying it exactly is how that would have happened

rows.surface: a keyboard reaches every operation the pointer reaches
rows.covered_by: the canon binds no key at all and reads two modifiers only inside pointer drags; this tree gives each composite one tab stop and a cursor inside it. ★ This row is NOT a removal instruction — the canon is the thing to reproduce, not a ceiling
